critique.evidence: Desktop has a cohesive, polished cyber-defense aesthetic: strong oversized headline, restrained dark grid, crisp cyan/red accents, consistent borders, and clear section hierarchy. Tablet remains attractive but the atlas columns visibly run beyond the panel and are cut off at the right edge. Mobile is not demo-ready aesthetically: the kill-chain graphic is clipped on both sides, column headings and cards disappear beyond the viewport, and the fixed-width data layout creates an incomplete, cramped composition. Several labels and JSON text are also extremely small, weakening readability despite otherwise consistent styling.
critique.fix: Create a true narrow-screen atlas presentation instead of clipping the desktop canvas: use a labeled horizontal scroller with visible affordance or convert stages into stacked/accordion sections, fit the kill-chain diagram to width, and prevent partial columns at viewport edges. Increase mobile metadata/code type slightly, add breathing room around dense cards, and preserve the strong desktop hierarchy across tablet and mobile.
